answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The echo multiplier is published, charged in whisper, and sable lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4834 identities would post 3519 proofs and burn roughly 85 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
